title: Marie Antoinette Never Said "Let Them Eat Cake" #shorts
description:
"Let them eat cake" is history's most famous quote that nobody can pin on Marie Antoinette.

The line comes from Rousseau's Confessions, written around 1765, about "a great princess" — and he wrote brioche, not cake. In 1765 Marie Antoinette was nine and living in Austria. Revolutionary pamphlets made her the villain, and the quote got pinned on her.

Animated, voiced and scored in code. Narration is a synthetic (text-to-speech) voice.

title: Einstein Never Failed Maths #shorts
description:
Everyone's heard that Einstein failed maths. He didn't.

He'd taught himself calculus by about 15, and when a 1935 newspaper column claimed he flunked, he said: "I never failed in mathematics." He did fail one university entrance exam — at 16, two years early — acing maths and physics but missing the general subjects. A year later he got in. One theory for the myth: his Swiss school's grading scale, where 6 was the top mark.

title: The Iron Maiden Probably Isn't Medieval #shorts
description:
The iron maiden is the most famous medieval torture device — and there's no medieval record of one.

The story traces back to a 1793 claim by the German writer Johann Philipp Siebenkees about an execution in 1515, with no sources. In the 1800s, museums wanted one, so people assembled them from old armour and spare parts. The famous Nuremberg iron maiden was destroyed in a 1944 bombing raid; copies still sit in museums.

title: Did Medieval People Really Die at 30? #shorts
description:
Medieval life expectancy was around 30 — but that's an average, not a lifespan.

High child mortality dragged the average way down. People who made it to adulthood often reached their 50s, 60s or 70s, and Eleanor of Aquitaine lived to about 80. Average: 30. Adults: much older.
